text.tspan: The numbers show the (constant) value to be written and also the order of writes.
In the SD case the write buffer size is set to 11 bricks.
1. 18 bricks (lower half of survey) set to all constant 1. No physical bricks allocated.
Expected file size SD (1, 0*) counting in number of bricks, with the asterisk signifying
the open segment not yet written to SD. The first segment contains the header.
For local files the size will be 1 brick.
2. 10 of 12 bricks need r/m/w, 2 bricks written fully to constant value 2.
The previous content is sometimes constant (upper part of survey) and sometimes
unset. 10 physical bricks need to be allocated in segment 1.
Expected file size SD (1, 10*) local 11.
3. 10 bricks already containing non-const data get updated. In the SD case all these
are inside the open segment so they don't need re-allocation. 2 bricks have their
constant value changed from 2 to 3. No new physical bricks allocated in either case.
Expected file size (1, 10*) local 11.
4. 6 new bricks allocated. In the SD case the segment size is only 11 bricks so 5 of
these end up in a new segment.
Expected file size SD (1, 11, 5*) local (17).
5. 12 bricks updated again, the same bricks touched by writes 2 and 3.
In the SD case all the 10 bricks with non constant data are in closed segment 1,
so new physical bricks need to be allocated for these and the old ones abandoned.
The two constant-value bricks still do not need any storage.
Expected file size SD (1, 11, 11, 4*) local (17) since there is no waste in the local case.
6. 6 bricks set to constant values. Note that the survey size is not a multiple of 64.
I only write up to the survey edge. The system is supposed to be smart enough to set
the padding bytes equal to the constant value in the rest of the brick, so these 5 won't
take up space in the file. The last brick will take up space since it contains mixed
values. The padding is now set differently.
Expected file size SD (1, 11, 11, 5*) local (18).
7. One full brick is set to constant value 7. But since the brick has previously contained
non-constant data it will still consume space, to avoid losing that disk block.
NOTE: in the SD case the block is lost anyway since it is in a closed segment.
So in that case the brick might as well be changed. For implementation reasons
I don't think I'll bother.
Expected file size SD (1, 11, 11, 6*) local (18).
Test file for the read/modify/write feature.
Survey edge
Padding added by system
